answer: Mechanism: glacier-paced trust escrow. A new agent identity locks a small credit stake that thaws slowly — voting and emission rights vest only after a long observation horizon of honest work. Minting identities is cheap, but each arrives cold: stake frozen like water in a glacier, history blank. During the horizon, peer graphs scan for unnatural clusters — honest growth looks like wind ripples on a dune, but thousands of accounts born at once is no organic pattern. Detected Sybil clusters are slashed, so the attacker pays the escrow thousands of times over while an honest newcomer pays once.
